body:
This is an effect of how Gradle compiles Java and Kotlin code separately. I added an extra debug print to `SplitPackageProcessor` and here's what I got:

```
2025-06-20 09:41:48,221 WARN  [io.qua.arc.dep.SplitPackageProcessor] (build-38) org.acme.lib:
2025-06-20 09:41:48,221 WARN  [io.qua.arc.dep.SplitPackageProcessor] (build-38) - [paths: /home/lthon/tmp/quarkus-reproducer/lib/build/classes/java/main;]
2025-06-20 09:41:48,221 WARN  [io.qua.arc.dep.SplitPackageProcessor] (build-38) - [paths: /home/lthon/tmp/quarkus-reproducer/lib/build/classes/kotlin/main;]
```
I know it's hacky, but wouldn't it make sense to check for this specific scenario, as it's terribly uncommon?

I personally think that in Kotlin projects, a decent chunk of them are in fact mixed Java/Kotlin projects, so this probably isn't totally uncommon. I don't remember exactly how the check works, but I recall we figure out there's a split package because there's multiple sources, and proceed to fill the set of artifacts. We should be able to check that if the set of artifacts in fact only has 1 element and not print the warning in that case.
Sorry, I meant `it's NOT terribly uncommon` :)

@rodcheater in your reproducer how would I configure Gradle to use Quarkus built from `main` (version `999-SNAPSHOT`)? I tried the usual ways I know of, but due to some Gradle specific thing I am not aware of, I couldn't get it to work.

@geoand In `settings.gradle` set the Quarkus version to `999-SNAPSHOT` and add `mavenLocal()` before `mavenCentral()` in the set of repositories in `dependencyResolutionManagement`. (I’ve already got Maven local in the plugin repositories for some reason.)
I tried that and it didn't work, but I'll give it another shot
